subject: Civil Engineering
title: Site Layout and Logistics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Site Layout and Logistics.

hook.text: Where do materials go? Where do workers park? Where does the crane sit? Layout decides it all.

buildup.text: The site logistics plan positions storage, access roads, offices, and hoisting equipment.

discovery.text: Material laydown areas must be close to installation points — moving materials twice wastes time.

twist.text: Urban sites have almost no laydown space — just-in-time delivery replaces on-site storage.

climax.text: Site layout evolves as the building rises — early phases need open ground, later phases need lifts.

punchline.text: A well-planned site flows. A poorly planned site chokes on its own congestion.

quiz.question: Why do urban construction sites use just-in-time delivery?
options: It's always cheaper than storing materials on site
Urban sites lack space for material storage, so deliveries arrive only when needed
City regulations prohibit storing any construction materials outdoors
